about.text: The dried fermented-milk cheese of the Kazakhs and other Central Asian nomads; the name comes from the Turkic word for ‘dry’. Milk is soured with yoghurt from an earlier batch, boiled, and the curd pressed in cloth, salted, rolled into small balls and sun-dried for up to two weeks. It keeps for over a year.
